chunks: First: Ali ibn al-Hasan ibn Faddal from Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Najran and Sindi ibn Muhammad from Asim ibn Humayd al-Hannat from Muhammad ibn Qays, who said: The Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) ruled in the case of a man who killed his mother, saying: If it was accidental, he inherits her; and if he killed her intentionally, he does not inherit her. Second: Al-Saffar from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn ibn Abi al-Khattab from Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Najran from Abd Allah ibn Sinan, who said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a man who killed his mother, does he inherit her? He said: If it was accidental, he inherits her; and if it was intentional, he does not inherit her.

As for what Ali ibn al-Hasan ibn Faddal narrated, saying: A man narrated to us from Muhammad ibn Sinan from Hammad ibn Uthman; and Muhammad ibn Ya'qub narrated from al-Husayn ibn Muhammad from Ali ibn Muhammad from some of his companions from Hammad ibn Uthman from Fudayl ibn Yasar from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: A man is not killed for his son, and the son is killed for his father if he killed his father, and a man does not inherit a man if he killed him, even if it was accidental. This does not contradict the first two reports for two reasons: one is that we may attribute it to a form of precautionary dissimulation (takiyyah), because among the general public (Sunnis) there are those who say that the killer does not inherit regardless of whether it was intentional or accidental. The other reason is that we may attribute it to what our Sheikh (peace be upon him) went to in reconciling these reports, namely that the killer by accident does not inherit from the blood money itself but inherits from what is other than it. This is a close interpretation. As for the reports we cited in our Great Book stating that the killer does not inherit, it is appropriate to specify them to the first two reports, and we say: The killer does not inherit except if it was accidental, so that the practice is upon all the narrations and nothing is dropped from them.
ai.seo_question: Does a son who kills his mother inherit her estate?
ai.summary: This narration from *Al-Istibsar* establishes the principle that a son who kills his mother is barred from inheritance if the act is intentional (*qatl al-'amd*), but retains his share if accidental (*qatl al-khata'*). Shaykh al-Tusi reconciles apparent contradictions in the reports by distinguishing between inheriting the estate's assets versus the specific *diyah* (blood money), or by attributing the stricter view to *taqiyya* to align with Sunni jurisprudence, thereby preserving the validity of all transmitted traditions.
